product_brief: Zero-trust and zero-knowledge identity security and Privileged Access Management (PAM) platform.
pqc_capability_description: Integrated NIST-approved Kyber key encapsulation mechanism using a hybrid approach combining elliptic curve cryptography with Kyber. Live in backend APIs and Commander tool; phased expansion planned. Secures client-server authentication and encrypted data-in-transit.
primary_platforms: Backend APIs, Keeper Commander, mobile platforms (coming soon)
regulatory_status: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, FedRAMP High Authorization, GovRAMP High Authorization, FIPS 140-3 validation
pqc_roadmap_details: Phased expansion across the platform; mobile platforms coming soon.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Delivered automatically as customers upgrade to the latest release; requires no configuration changes or user action; maintains backward compatibility.

product_brief: Complete credential security platform unifying credential protection and password management with patented zero-knowledge security.
pqc_capability_description: Dashlane has conceived a Proof-of-Concept to study PQC integration. They plan to use new Post-Quantum standards (CRYSTALS-Kyber, CRYSTALS-Dilithium, Falcon, SPHINCS+) as soon as possible once standardized. They currently operate using a hybrid mode (Pre-Quantum like RSA and Post-Quantum like CRYSTALS-Kyber) in their PoC. They released an open-source project `pqc.js` with WebAssembly/JS bindings for NIST finalists to test migration.
key_management_model: Hybrid mode (combining Pre-Quantum and Post-Quantum algorithms)
license: Open Source (for pqc.js project); Commercial (for Dashlane platform)
pqc_roadmap_details: Plan to use new Post-Quantum standards (CRYSTALS-Kyber, CRYSTALS-Dilithium, Falcon, SPHINCS+) as soon as possible once standardized. Currently using a hybrid mode in Proof-of-Concept.

product_brief: India’s first quantum-safe messaging and collaboration platform for enterprises, offering web and mobile access with NIST-aligned PQC.
pqc_capability_description: QVerse is described as "India’s first quantum-safe messaging platform" and "quantum-safe SaaS". It uses "NIST-aligned post-quantum algorithms", specifically "CRYSTALS-Kyber" (lattice-based cryptography) for Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM). It is deployed in BFSI and Defence sectors.
target_industries: BFSI, Healthcare, Telecom, Defence, Critical Infrastructure, Energy, Government

product_brief: Secure messaging service working with IBM to implement quantum-safe cryptography into its messaging system.
pqc_capability_description: Threema is working with IBM to implement quantum-safe cryptography. They are exploring how to implement ML-KEM (a key encapsulation mechanism selected for general encryption) into their messaging system. The collaboration aims to lay the foundation for quantum-secure communication.
pqc_roadmap_details: Threema is collaborating with IBM to explore the implementation of ML-KEM into its messaging system to achieve quantum-safe communication.

product_brief: Secure messaging application with no user identifiers, supporting Android, iOS, and desktop platforms.
A proposed upgrade to the Session Protocol introducing Perfect Forward Secrecy, Post-Quantum Cryptography, and improved linked device management.
pqc_capability_description: The V2 protocol plans to utilize ML-KEM (previously CRYSTALS-Kyber), a standardized post-quantum Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM), to establish secure shared secrets. This aims to protect against "harvest now, decrypt later" attacks by future quantum adversaries. The protocol is currently in the design phase, with detailed specifications expected in 2026.
crypto_primitives: Elliptic curve cryptography (current V1); ML-KEM (CRYSTALS-Kyber) (planned for V2)
key_management_model: Rotating Key Pairs (per-device and per-account); Long-Term Key (LTK) in V1; private keys stored on-device and never shared between linked devices in V2.
architecture_type: Application-layer cryptographic protocol; decentralized network using onion-routing.
pqc_roadmap_details: Detailed specifications of the V2 protocol are planned to be released in 2026 as it undergoes additional stages of review. The protocol intends to use ML-KEM for key encapsulation.
signature_schemes: Not stated (Text mentions LTK for encryption/authorization in V1 and ML-KEM for key establishment in V2, but does not explicitly name signature algorithms like Ed25519 or ECDSA)

product_brief: The world's first quantum-safe, secure, end-to-end encrypted messaging app for enterprise use.
pqc_capability_description: Offers end-to-end quantum-resistant encryption protecting every message. Built on post-quantum cryptographic algorithms that resist both classical and quantum attacks.

product_brief: Industry’s first Quantum-Proof Secure Communication Platform powered by ML-KEM 1024 encryption.
pqc_capability_description: Powered by ML-KEM 1024 (Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism - an evolution of CRYSTALS-Kyber) quantum-safe encryption. Features a Rust-based ML-KEM 1024 Implementation offering memory safety, high security, and cross-platform compatibility. Includes crypto-agile architecture for seamless transition to quantum-safe cryptography while maintaining backward compatibility for existing encrypted data.
key_management_model: Automated updates of cryptographic algorithms, keys, and certificates; modular architecture isolating cryptographic algorithms.
architecture_type: Crypto-agile architecture with modular isolation of cryptographic algorithms.
target_industries: Enterprise, Healthcare, Scientific research, Artificial intelligence
pqc_roadmap_details: N/A (Product is already implemented with ML-KEM 1024)
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Backward compatibility enabled for seamless interaction between systems with new quantum-proof encryption and legacy systems; automated updates ensure continuous updates of cryptographic algorithms, keys, and certificates.

product_brief: Dual-layer, quantum-resistant encryption protecting sensitive communications using hybrid PQC algorithms.
pqc_capability_description: Implements a dual-algorithm hybrid approach combining Crystals Kyber (lattice-based) and Classic McEliece (code-based) for layered defense. Includes an Agile Post-Quantum crypto layer for easy algorithm replacement. Integrates classical AES-256 and ECDH for backward compatibility.
crypto_primitives: Crystals Kyber, Classic McEliece, AES-256, ECDH
pqc_roadmap_details: 2021: Launch of first secure comms app with PQC. 2023: Introduction of Agile Post-Quantum Crypto Layer. 2025: Launch of Layered Post-Quantum Cryptography (Kyber + McEliece). Upcoming: Enhanced upgrades with advanced quantum-resistant improvements.
testing_&_validation_methods: NIST Validated, NATO Certified, FIPS 140-3 Level 3 Certified, extensive cryptanalytic review
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Optimized for mobile and embedded devices
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Backward compatibility maintained via classical encryption integration; Agile framework allows seamless algorithm updates without complete system overhauls

product_brief: A privacy-focused, open-source collaborative platform with end-to-end encryption for documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.
pqc_capability_description: Post-quantum cryptography research is underway following a 6-month internship. The Crystals suite (ML-KEM and ML-DSA) was chosen for integration due to speed and security. Crypto-agility has been added to facilitate switching cryptographic libraries. Technical and usability blockers remain before rollout.
primary_platforms: Web, Mobile (iOS/Android via Murena Vault integration)
pqc_roadmap_details: Selected Crystals suite (ML-KEM and ML-DSA) for PQC integration. Work is in the research/prototype phase with technical and usability blockers to overcome before rollout. Crypto-agility refactor completed to support future library switching.

testing_&_validation_methods: KAT (Known Answer Tests) support mentioned ("correction in tree operations KAT"); interoperability testing mentioned ("interop_client"); validation checks and tests mentioned.
